newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu posts record 96/97 group profit.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu posts record 96/97 group profit.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday its groups profits and sales jumped to their highest levels ever in the last business year, buoyed by strong sales of recreational vehicles.

The nation's second-biggest minicar maker said its group net profit surged 167.5 percent to a record 19.73 billion yen in the year ended in March, surpassing its previous record marked the year before.
Its group sales also rose to a record 909.56 billion yen, surpassing the previous record of 875 billion yen marked in 1992/93.
"Strong domestic demand for new recreational vehicles -- the 660cc Move and the compact Pyzar -- contributed to the record result," a Daihatsu spokesman told Reuters.
Daihatsu started exporting the Move and the Pyzar to Europe last January and they have met with good demand, he said. The export version of the Move is equipped with an 850cc engine.
Last Wednesday, Daihatsu, owned 33.4 percent by Toyota Motor Corp, announced a parent net profit of 6.39 billion yen in 1996/97, up 58.9 percent from a year earlier.
